reviewer: independent_review: source-and-reference review; separate from benchmark author

cases.reason: No overwrite of captured wrapper through *a, no redirected completion or replacement counter trace.
No caller-local pointer rebinding and preserved original receiver comparison.

findings.reason: Without a same-generation condition an admitted nil/non-nil return does not necessarily update success/failure counters: afterRequest discards an outcome after intervening generation change (gobreaker.go:293-301). Initial behavior under an unchanged generation and ordinary default settings is correct.

Defer covers request and IsSuccessful panic, afterRequest gates outcome on generation and Goexit bypasses reporting; cancellation classified as failure under default classifier subject to the explicitly noted generation gate.
currentState runs before generation check, Counts only reads current counters, deadline transition is lazy; first case explicitly assumes no intervening state change.
Same-generation duplicate reports are not guarded; either success threshold or failure changes generation so later report is ignored.
Default max=1, half-open expiry zero and absent callback leave cap occupied; current-generation result can change state.
setState mutates state and clears counts while caller holds mutex, invokes callback synchronously; State/Counts lock same mutex, Name does not.
